chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Abdullah ibn Hilal who said:

I complained to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the separation of our wealth and what had entered upon us (as a result of it). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is upon you with the supplication while you are prostrating, for the closest of what the servant can happen to be to Allah is when he is prostrating'.

He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'So shall I supplicate during the Obligatory (Salat) and specify my need?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had done that, and he (peace be upon him) supplicated against a people with their names and the names of their fathers; and Ali (peace be upon him) did so after him (peace be upon him and his family)'.
ai.seo_question: When is the best time to make du'a for specific needs according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the theological principle that sujūd is the pinnacle of proximity to the Divine, validating the practice of personalizing supplications within obligatory prayers. The Imam’s citation of the Prophet and Imam Ali establishes a strong Shia precedent for naming specific individuals and needs, reinforcing the continuity of prophetic tradition in private devotion.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hajjal, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Sa’albat Bin Maymoun, from Abdullah Bin Hilal who said,

‘I complained to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> of the separation of our wealth and what had entered upon us (as a result of it)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is upon you with the supplication while you are prostrating, for the closest of what the servant can happen to be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is when he is prostrating’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘So shall I supplicate during the Obligatory (Salāt) and specify my need?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes. Rasool-Allahsaww had done that, and hesaww supplicated against a people with their names and the names of their fathers; and Aliasws did so after himsaww’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hajjal from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from ‘Abd Allah ibn Hilal who has said the following:

“I once complained before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the difficulties we faced and deprivation from our belongings. He (the Imam) said, ‘You must plead (before Allah) when you are in Sajdah (prostration) position; the nearest position to Allah for a servant of Allah is one’s position in Sajdah (prostration).’

I then asked, ‘Can I plead (before Allah) in obligatory Salah (prayer) and mention my needs?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘Yes, you can do so; the Messenger of Allah had done so. He pleaded (before Allah) against a people and mentioned their names and the names of their fathers. After him Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, also had done so.’” (Hadith 11 is best explained in the form of fatwa.)
